result: In 30 ME/CFS patients labelled with psychogenic pseudosyncope vs 30 matched ME/CFS controls, extracranial Doppler CBF fell 39% vs 25% at end tilt, with no HR or BP differences.
reason: Same extracranial Doppler tilt CBF measure; adds a frequent-syncope subgroup with larger fall; no healthy controls.

result: In 30 ME/CFS patients labelled with psychogenic pseudosyncope vs 30 matched ME/CFS controls, extracranial Doppler CBF fell 39% vs 25% at end tilt, with no HR or BP differences.
reason: Same measure, same clinic; adds a subgroup with larger CBF fall despite similar HR/BP.

result: Re-analysis of exercise-provocation fMRI (31 HC, 36 ME/CFS, 78 GWI): task activation in midbrain arousal nuclei (PAG, raphe, locus coeruleus, parabrachial) rose after submaximal exercise in ME/CFS, fell in GWI, and was unchanged in controls.
reason: Same pre/post-exercise cognitive-task fMRI design; adds increased post-exertion recruitment in midbrain nuclei from a different team (Washington 2020 data).

result: Pre-exercise, ME/CFS showed less left pedunculotegmental activation than controls during cognition; post-exercise, midbrain arousal nuclei activation rose in ME/CFS (31 HC, 36 ME/CFS, 78 GWI).
reason: Altered brainstem/midbrain task signal fits the finding's 'altered signal' scope; seed-based re-analysis, modest weight.

result: In 50 mild COVID-19 survivors vs 28 uninfected villagers with pre-pandemic baselines, MoCA decline seen at 6 months appeared to improve by 18 months.
reason: MoCA screening in a post-COVID village cohort does not test the ME/CFS domain-specific deficits claimed; no atlas finding on long COVID cognitive trajectory.

result: 10 long COVID patients (all POTS on tilt), 20 ME/CFS-POTS, 20 ME/CFS-normal-HR/BP and 10 HC: CBF and cardiac index fell more in all patient groups than HC, with larger CBF fall in long COVID than in normal-response ME/CFS.
reason: Same tilt CBF measure but from the same Dutch clinic in a small sample; main addition is the long COVID version, so extends rather than replicates.

result: 10 long COVID patients (all POTS on tilt), 20 ME/CFS-POTS, 20 ME/CFS-normal-HR/BP and 10 HC: CBF and cardiac index fell more in all patient groups than HC, with larger CBF fall in long COVID than in normal-response ME/CFS.
reason: Same clinic and method, not an independent cohort; adds long COVID comparison, so extends.

result: Non-invasive CPET in 41 PASC patients with unexplained dyspnoea: mean peak VO2 77% predicted (58.5% below 80%), 88% had ventilatory abnormalities (dysfunctional breathing n=26, raised VE/VCO2 n=17, resting PetCO2 33.5 mmHg/hypocapnia).
reason: No invasive CPET or oxygen-extraction measure; findings are dysfunctional breathing/hypocapnia and low peak VO2 in long COVID, uncontrolled.

result: Non-invasive CPET in 41 PASC patients: 88% had ventilatory abnormalities including dysfunctional breathing (n=26), raised VE/VCO2 (n=17) and resting hypocapnia (PetCO2 33.5 mmHg).
reason: Measures resting and exercise hypocapnia/dysfunctional breathing, not orthostatic hypocapnia or its link to CBF; vascular-hypocapnia covers exercise dysfunctional breathing; long COVID, no controls.

result: 3T PCASL in 31 ME/CFS vs 48 HC showed resting hypoperfusion in anterior cingulate, putamen, pallidum and anterior ventral insula, and lower ACC rCBF correlated with symptom severity.
reason: Independent ASL cohort reproducing lower resting rCBF incl. anterior cingulate (as Shungu 2012); OI status not recorded.
